notes: Texas has no personal income tax, so self-employment income is subject only to federal income and self-employment tax.

A Texas LLC (including a single-member LLC taxed as a sole proprietorship) is a taxable entity for the franchise tax, but owes no tax when annualized total revenue is at or below the no-tax-due threshold ($2,650,000 for 2026 and 2027 reports); it must still file a Public Information Report or Ownership Information Report each year by May 15. Sole proprietors without an LLC are not subject.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $300 Certificate of Formation (Form 205, Texas Secretary of State).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: None with the Secretary of State. LLCs must file a free franchise tax Public Information Report (or Ownership Information Report) with the Comptroller every year by May 15.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: Franchise tax applies to LLCs (including single-member LLCs) but no tax is due if annualized total revenue is at or below $2,650,000 (2026 and 2027 reports); above that, 0.75% of taxable margin (0.375% for retail/wholesale). No minimum tax. Sole proprietorships are not subject.
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: None for a typical freelancer below the franchise tax threshold (the Texas franchise tax is a margin tax that only applies to LLCs above $2,650,000 in revenue).
